pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Many Weapons is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Enter throws, and what it throws depends on what you are carrying: a flame if you have one, otherwise a star, otherwise it only shrugs. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Touch a sack to fill it. Nothing in this game can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: Empty Hands
pages.html:
Level 1: Empty Hands

NOTHING TO THROW YET. ENTER JUST SHRUGS is the first sign. Press Enter before you have touched anything: Lena shrugs and a low blip plays, and nothing flies. TOUCH THE POUCH FOR TWO STARS. ENTER THROWS ONE comes next. Walk into the sack and you hold two stars; each press of Enter throws one the way you last walked, to pop a mint green gumdrop. Three gumdrops stand in a row, so the third one needs more than two stars. OUT OF STARS? ENTER SHRUGS AGAIN. THE POUCH FILLS UP says what to do: go back. About four seconds after you took them, the sack is full again.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Three sequences on one key. Open hero.chr in the Character tab. Three sequences are on the Enter key: the flame (sequence 14), the star (15) and the shrug (17). When you press the key, the game starts the first one in that list that is switched on and has uses left. Nothing picks a weapon; the list order and the counts decide.
  • Uses left. Each of these sequences has a repetition counter with its own number: 14 for the flame, 15 for the star. The hero starts with both at 0, so only the shrug, which is never used up, can run. Each throw takes one off.
  • A pouch adds to a counter. Open mw.mbl in the Monster Blocks tab: the star pouch picture has Effect 15 and Amount 2. Touching it adds 2 to counter 15. The sack is a monster, mw.mon number 8, with power 50 (less than the hero's 100), so touching it takes it, and it "becomes" the empty sack.
  • Filling up again. The empty sack is monster 9. It has power 100, so touching it takes nothing, and a lifetime of 72 ticks (about four seconds). When that is up it becomes the full sack again. A monster's clock starts when it is born, which is why this works and a timed block would not: every copy of a block shares one clock.
  • The gumdrops. Monster 6 has power 110 and a star has 120, so a star pops it and the hero gets its 50 points.
  • The map. Open one.map: ground, three gumdrops and a sack. A scene link joins the door at the right to the next level in mw.gam.

pages.head: Level 2: Star or Flame
pages.html:
Level 2: Star or Flame

A STAR CAN'T MELT FROST. TAKE STARS AND TRY comes first. Take the star pouch, walk up to the frosty grump in the tunnel and press Enter: the star is used up and the grump does not move. A FLAME CAN. JUMP UP TO THE FLAME POUCH points up at a ledge. Jump up through it, stand on it and you hold two flames. FLAMES GO FIRST. WHEN THEY ARE GONE, ENTER THROWS A STAR says the rest: you still have a star in your pocket, but the first two presses of Enter throw flames, and each melts one grump. The third press throws a star, which pops the gumdrop past the tunnel.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The order of the list is the order of the weapons. The flame is sequence 14 and the star is 15, so while both counters are above 0 the flame wins. Swap their numbers in the Character tab and the star would go first.
  • Power decides who wins. Open mw.mon. The frosty grump (monster 7) has power 150. A star has 120 and loses to it; a flame has 200 and wins. A monster the hero throws is used up whatever it hits, so a losing star simply vanishes, but the grump stays.
  • Solid. Open mw.mbl: the grump's pictures are solid on every side, so Lena cannot walk through it. It fills a tunnel two blocks high, so they cannot go over or under it either.
  • The ledge. In two.map the flame pouch sits one block above a row of planks, which Lena can jump up through and stand on. The star pouch is on the ground, so the flame is the harder to reach.
  • Counters carry on. A star left in your pocket at the end of level 1 is still there in level 2; the counters belong to the hero, not the level.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. The last door links to the The End scene in mw.gam.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot show how many are left. The counters are not drawn anywhere on their own. Show a count with pictures or signs, as another Starter does.
  • It cannot pick a weapon by name. There is no weapon menu: Enter runs the first sequence on the key that is switched on and has uses left. To choose, change the counts or the order.
  • It has no limit on shots in the air. Nothing stops a second star leaving before the first lands. The only limits are the toss taking a moment, and the monster slots: a game has no more than 200 monsters, and only 50 are drawn at once.
  • A thrown weapon flies one way. It goes the way the hero last walked, in a straight line, and dies when it hits a wall or its lifetime is up.
  • Counters cannot have a limit. A pouch adds to a counter every time it is touched, so a game with no pause between pouches could stack them up. Here the sack is empty for a few seconds.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Give a pouch more: change its Amount in the Monster Blocks tab.
  • Swap the flame's and the star's numbers on the Character tab, and see which one Enter throws first.
  • Draw a third weapon, such as a snowball, add a sequence for it on the same key, and make a pouch for it.
  • Change a power: a star at 160 melts the frosty grump.
  • Make a pouch refill faster or slower by changing the empty sack's lifetime.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a red beanie has two short levels to cross and a pocketful of pouches to find. A pouch of stars, a pouch of flames, a mint green gumdrop and a frosty grump in a narrow way. Enter is the only throwing key, and what it throws depends on what you are carrying. Signs say what each level shows, and the manual says how each is made.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
One key throws a flame, a star or nothing: each weapon is a sequence that counts its own uses
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Two short levels about one key that throws different things. A pouch of stars and a pouch of flames fill counters, and Enter throws a flame if there is one, a star if there is not, and nothing when there is neither. A star pops a mint green gumdrop but cannot melt a frosty grump; a flame can. Each weapon is a sequence in the character file. Signs explain each idea, and every level has a page on how it is made.

28.long: Throw a flame if you have one, a star if you do not, and shrug if you have neither.

57.long: Jump. Steer with Left and Right while you are in the air.

2.long: Throw a flame or a star, the way you last walked.

counters.15: Stars: how many Enter can throw after the flames. A star pouch adds to it.
